qs.q:
Shopkeepers — Which person talks about a shopkeeper who…

A=Alice (foreign owner, worked very hard, open Sundays, modern security cameras, not pricey, late-night licence rejected)
B=Ben (old-fashioned counter, Mrs Smith extended credit, accused of overcharging, shop looked empty but perfectly organised)
C=Cathy (sweet shop, fierce woman, refused credit, paranoid about shoplifting — max 4 at time, failing eyesight)
D=Don (Mr Field, smart, organised charity events, prosecuted for selling tobacco to minors, worked until midnight)
E=Eve (curious shop, bare shelves, pleasant gossip, invested money, had ramp for wheelchair access)
F=Frank (expensive, reserved owner, didn't chat, difficult to be accepted by locals, emigrated to France)

0. had a shop with modern equipment? [A=Alice: 'security cameras']
1. had a shop that was rather expensive?
2. had very little on sale in their store?
3. appeared different from how they really were?
4. liked to talk with customers?
5. was an immigrant?
6. was worried about shoplifting?
7. had a reputation for cheating customers?
8. did not fit into the community?
9. had late opening hours?
10. had a shop that appeared well organised?
11. had a physical disability?
12. sometimes let customers pay later?
items: 1 — had a shop that was rather expensive?
2 — had very little on sale in their store?
3 — appeared different from how they really were?
7 — had a reputation for cheating customers?
8 — did not fit into the community?
10 — had a shop that appeared well organised?

qs.q:
A Quieter Life

"Our PRIMARY MOTIVATION was to provide a SECURE ENVIRONMENT for the four of us."

What was Guy's main reason for moving?
A Living in the city was too expensive.
B His family loved the spectacular beauty of the island.
C He wanted his family to live somewhere safe.
D It allowed him to spend more time with his children.
opts: Living in the city was too expensive.
His family loved the spectacular beauty of the island.
He wanted his family to live somewhere safe.
It allowed him to spend more time with his children.

qs.q:
A Quieter Life

"We're also quite a WAY FROM THE MAINLAND, which can be an INCONVENIENCE SOMETIMES."

What does Guy complain about in the second paragraph?
A The cost of housing on the island.
B The number of newcomers.
C The isolation of the place.
D The amount of work he does.
opts: The cost of housing on the island.
The amount of work he does.

qs.q:
A Quieter Life

"A massive ALL-ROUND ADJUSTMENT IS REQUIRED and it DOES NOT OCCUR OVERNIGHT."

What does Guy say you must be realistic about if you move to an island?
A You will have less money.
B It takes time to adapt.
C The way of life is conservative.
D There is less privacy.
opts: The way of life is conservative.

qs.q:
A Quieter Life

"If you ask me, it's the SHORT DAYS that take the MOST GETTING USED TO."

What does Guy find most difficult about winter on the island?
A Not going out much.
B The lack of daylight.
C The freezing temperatures.
D The absence of entertainment.

A Quieter Life

"I feel a certain sense of PRIDE at having successfully made the transition and living in an unspoilt, clean environment."

How does Guy's new life make him feel?
A Satisfied.
B Relaxed.
C Healthier.
D Optimistic.

A Quieter Life

"It all BOILS DOWN TO THE KIND OF PERSON YOU ARE."

What would Guy say about downshifting?
A 'It's the answer to the problems of modern life.'
B 'It will be done by more people in the future.'
C 'It is very good for the environment.'
D 'It isn't a good solution for everybody.'
opts: 'It's the answer to the problems of modern life.'
'It will be done by more people in the future.'
'It is very good for the environment.'
'It isn't a good solution for everybody.'

B That is, until a guy starts talking to me.
C Nor do I have the ability to go for half an hour without blinking.
D So it's not unknown for performers to claim the best ones as early as 3am, which occasionally leads to violence.

H — you have to be in control of every muscle
